findings.problem: In headless Chromium on the loaded machine, the beach ball takes 138-154 ms to build cold, which is right at the ~150 ms limit (soccer 120-138 ms, baseball 121-135 ms and bowling 116-128 ms also have little headroom). In the beach colour bake (balls.js lines 1630-1640, 2048x1024), each pixel makes several small arrays: geom() returns an object, and every mix3 call and every colour literal allocates a new array. That is several million short-lived objects. The loop alone takes about 40 ms in node (scratchpad/r4rv/beachbench.mjs). The 8 MB result then goes through putImageData into a 2D canvas.
findings.fix: In the beach colour bake, work in scalar r, g, b. Take thp and inCap once per row from p.y. Take k and dSeam from p.x and p.st without the geom() object. Do each mix as `r += (255 - r) * w` and so on, with no arrays. That should bring the loop to about 10 ms. Optional, and it helps every 2048-wide bake (soccer, billiard, bowling, ping-pong): skip the canvas round trip in texOf(canvasOf(W, H, o)). Instead make `new THREE.DataTexture(o, W, H)` with the rows baked bottom-up (or flip once), colorSpace SRGB, generateMipmaps true, minFilter LinearMipmapLinearFilter, wrapS Repeat, anisotropy 8. Re-time cold builds afterwards (mode=cost&only=steel-ball,beach-ball) and expect well under 100 ms.

findings.problem: The fuzz shells disappear at the edge of the ball, so its outline is the bare core: a clean, hard sphere edge with no felt fringe. At any size up to 67 mm it sits 2.4% of r inside the physics circle (0.8 mm at the default size; within tolerance). Shots: r4-rv-tennis-rim-b, r4-rv-tennis-limb. The cause is the fuzzFade term: fpx = length(fwidth(vAlphaMapUv * [1536, 768])) becomes large where the surface is seen edge-on, because the texel footprint stretches along one axis there, so the shell alpha fades to 0 exactly where the fibres should form the outline. A real tennis ball shows a fuzzy halo. Together with the engine's 0.9 mm contact skin, the default ball's lowest drawn point is 1.7 mm above the table.
findings.fix: In bm() for fuzzFade, base the fade on the smaller axis of the footprint: `vec2 fw = fwidth(vAlphaMapUv * vec2(1536.0, 768.0)); float fpx = min(fw.x, fw.y);` and use that in place of length(fwidth(...)). The shells' flecks then survive at the edge, where the footprint is stretched along only one axis, and the felt tips form the outline (out to r). Check a front close-up at 67 mm and at 5 mm for sparkle at the edge; alpha-to-coverage should keep it soft.

findings.problem: A non-cubic block of ice looks like a cracked pane, not a block of ice. In iceInside(), the core and bubbles scale with s = min(w, h, d), but the feathers (pos.push(p[0] * w, p[1] * h, p[2] * d)) and the fracture sheet (sheetGeo(crackPoints(), w, h, d)) stretch with each dimension separately. So a flat or long block gets long, thin white streaks radiating from a dot in the middle, plus a large ring, over the dark shadow on the table seen through the ice. Visible at 0.2x0.05x0.1, 0.3x0.03x0.2, 0.5x0.1x0.3 and 1.0x0.02x0.3 (r3-blocks-r3-iceflat-1/2/3/5, r3-blocks-r3-ex-ice-cube-flat). The ice cube's own size handle changes width and height, so a user can reach these shapes directly. Default cubes and the ice wedge (which uses a cube of 1.8 rho) are fine.
findings.fix: In iceInside(w, h, d), build the feathers and the fracture in the same cube as the core. Feathers: pos.push(c[0] * s, c[1] * s - 0.12 * h, c[2] * s) for the centre and p[0] * s, p[1] * s - 0.12 * h, p[2] * s for each point (s = min(w, h, d), already computed there); key the geometry on s and h. Fracture: sheetGeo(crackPoints(), s, s, s, ...) offset down by 0.12 * h like the core. For a block longer than about 2.5 s, optionally repeat the core group (core, halo, feathers, bubbles) every 1.6 s along the long axis, as a long mould freezes a line of cloud. Then a 0.2x0.05x0.1 block shows one compact white cloud with short feathers, as real ice does.

The panel sag (-0.0009 * dent) and the fbm bumps ((fbm3(x*25, ...) - 0.5) * 0.0004, a 4 cm period) are fixed amounts. The edge radius min(0.0026, 0.1 * min) is 2.6 mm even on a 3 cm tall box, and the liner's mottling is magnified close up. So 5x3x4 and 10x6x8 cm boxes show puffy rounded edges and blotchy bumps (r3-blocks-r3-box-5-close, box-10-close, box-small). The minor-flap line also sits a fixed 3.5 mm below the top (hy - 0.0035), a third of the way down a 1 cm box. Boxes of 20 cm and larger look right.
findings.fix: In cardboardBox(): let k = clamp01(min(w, h, d) / 0.15). Use disp = -0.0009 * k * dent + (fbm3(...) - 0.5) * 0.0004 * k. Use an edge radius of min(0.0026, 0.04 * min(w, h, d)) for both geo and rr. Use a flap-line offset of hy - min(0.0035, 0.15 * H). The default 300x200x200 box is unchanged (k = 1).

In bucket():

findings.problem:
Standing on its blunt end, the egg stays up; a real egg falls over. The outline's blunt tip is a vertex, and the facet next to it, (-28.64, 0) to (-26.43, ±10.6), holds the centre of gravity: the foot of the perpendicular from it lands at t = 0.52 along that edge. The egg can therefore stand on that facet, tilted about 12 degrees off vertical. Drop tests through /api/simulate:
- Released between 70 and 110 degrees from 1.5 mm, 3 cm or 10 cm up, it settles standing at 78 or 102 degrees.
- Dropped from 10 or 30 cm at 36 angles, 3 of 36 end standing on the blunt end. One more rests tilted 48 degrees on the next facet (the t = 0.99 edge).
- At exactly ±90 degrees it balances on either tip for ever.
The minimum-size egg does the same. On the true curve the blunt tip's radius of curvature is 23.8 mm, less than the 27.5 mm from the tip to the centre of gravity, so the real egg is unstable on its end. With a vertex at the tip, any chord near the curve is stable unless the distance to the centre of gravity exceeds 2R (47.6 mm), so polygons cannot fix this within the 0.6 mm tolerance. My vertex search needed 1.5 mm of outline error and a 3 mm longer egg. Side note: a real (3D) egg rests at about 8.9 degrees, using the volume centroid at x = -1.80 mm, not 10.6. final.verdict:
Round 4 does not pass. The fixer's round-3 claims all hold. Three new major problems remain, and all three are in the group's own catalog builders: (1) the spring catapult's cocked arm starts inside the table, or inside its own base, across much of the slider range; (2) the spring bumper's "pushed_in" has no limit; (3) a spring-gate plank thicker than about 2 cm swings its corners up through its own hanger.

Fixer claims I checked and confirmed:
- Pulley-lift bail: the crown stays at the rope tie for pails 3 to 30 cm tall and 4 to 30 cm wide (r3-rv4-pl-h20-cu, pl-flat-cu, pl-def-top).
- Launcher and bounce pad at 6 cm wide: the springs stand 30 mm apart on separate seats (r3-rv4-sl-w6-cu*, bp-w6-cu).
- Thick chain: the links fill the outline (y -0.35 mm). The 3 to 6 mm ribbon chain reads as a real chain close up (hc-6-cu*, hc-thin-cu).
- Trampoline textures do not depend on size. Texture count stayed at 12 across width, depth and height sweeps. Rows are capped at 12.
- Hardwood lab masses look right at 50 g, 1.37 kg and 5 kg.
- Catapult stop grain matches the post. The arm visibly rests on the rubber cap at rest (sc-rest-olz, sc-min-olz).
- Wrecking-ball eye at 0.2 kg: the chain wire passes through the ring (wb-02-eye).
- The chain render hint is present. I agree that the swing and rope pendulum should stay rope: a lab pendulum hangs on cord, and the swing's seat is knotted through grommets.

Other checks:
- Texture count stays flat over sweeps of mass weight (steel and wood), pail size, chain thickness, wrecking-ball mass, catapult angle, spinner length and bumper height.
- No console warnings.
- Catalog cards now show the pulley wheels and ropes, the chain and the motor.

Tests and scenarios:
- test_rg PASS; test_mechanisms 29/29 PASS.
- Scenarios through /api/simulate: atwood OK, spring-launch goal met, trampoline OK. In wrecking-ball, brick 1 still never moves (that scene file is outside the group).

Cold build in headless Chromium with a Metal GPU: every item builds in 35 ms or less and 22.6k triangles or less at defaults, and 37 ms or less and 22.6k or less at extreme props.

Worst visual faults outside the group's files, unchanged:
- view3d still draws the Atwood machine and pulley lift with two toy wheels with '+' faces, and the ropes slant.
- The trampoline gets one spring per end, at z = 0, between hooks.
- The wrecking-ball chain is about 53k triangles (the scene is 76k).
- web/sim/catalog-mechanisms.js does not yet include the three round-3 Python edits.

findings.problem: build_catapult never checks that the cocked arm clears the floor. The arm's lowest corner (item frame: base top y = 0, table y = -0.02) is y_low = H0 - 0.7*L*sin(a) - (t/2)*cos(a). That corner is under the tabletop for a cocked angle over about 35° at the default arm and post, or for an arm over 0.54 m at the default 25°. Cocked 40°: the lip and arm end are 1.8 cm into the tabletop (r3-rv4-sc-c40-ol.png). Cocked 60°: the arm passes through its own base and 8 cm into the table (sc-c60-ol). Arm 1.2 m at 25°: the end is 21 cm under the tabletop (sc-a12-ol). /api/simulate warns 'Spring catapult starts inside Table top' in all three cases. The arm stays embedded for the whole hold (0 to 0.5 s), so a ball set in the cup would sit inside the table.
findings.fix: In build_catapult (catalog_mechanisms.py), right after reading P and t: H0 = max(P['post_height'], 0.7 * L * math.sin(a) + (t / 2) * math.cos(a) + 0.004). The post then grows just enough for the cocked arm's lowest corner to clear the base top by 4 mm. The arm's y, the pin anchor, the stop's y_top, the spring and the 'post' slab all already derive from H0, and the models read ctx.h, so nothing else changes. The defaults are unchanged (0.131 < 0.15), so test_mechanisms' throw is unchanged; re-run it. Mirror the line in web/sim/catalog-mechanisms.js build_catapult: const H0 = pymax(P.post_height, 0.7 * L * sin(a) + (t / 2) * cos(a) + 0.004). The alternative is to clamp a to the bisected root of y_low(a) = 0.004 and say so in the prop's help text.

findings.problem: build_bumper uses pushed_in with no limit. (1) At the default spring length 0.1, pushed_in 0.1 puts the plate flat on the wall. Both springs are drawn at zero length, which a real 10-turn coil of 1.9 mm wire (about 2.2 cm solid with its seats) cannot reach (r3-rv4-sb-push10-ol.png). (2) At rest 0.03 with pushed_in 0.06, the plate starts 15 mm inside the static wall, with the spring seats poking through both faces (sb-push-r3-ol). No warning is given because both are parts of the same item, and the engine fires the plate out at 3.9 m/s. (3) At pushed_in below -0.04 the plate stands past the shelf's end (the shelf is only rest + t + 0.04 long) and hangs in mid air (sb-pull10-*). Simulated at -0.1: at release the plate topples flat (angle 89° at 0.6 s).
findings.fix: In build_bumper: coils = max(5, min(24, int(rest / 0.01))) (what _spring draws); push = min(P['pushed_in'], rest - (coils * 0.002 + 0.004)), which leaves a closed coil plus the two seat lips; end = rest + max(0.0, -push) + t + 0.04, so the shelf always runs under the plate. The defaults are unchanged. Mirror both lines in web/sim/catalog-mechanisms.js build_bumper (line ~344): const push = pymin(P.pushed_in, rest - (pymax(5, pymin(24, Math.trunc(rest / 0.01))) * 0.002 + 0.004)); end = rest + pymax(0, -push) + t + 0.04.

findings.problem: The gate turns about the middle of its top end, so its top corners rise by (thickness/2)*sin|angle|. The hanger's underside is only 6 mm above the pin (_hanger(c, y=0.012)). Thickness 0.03 at the default 40° puts a corner 3.6 mm into the hanger. Thickness 0.04 at 40° (r3-rv4-sg-t4-hinge.png) and 0.1 at 60° (sg-t10-hinge, where the plank covers half the hanger) overlap the hanger outline. At the default 2 cm and 80° the overlap is 3.8 mm. The engine collides the two. With 0.1 thickness from 60°, the gate drops 18.6° in the first 50 ms after release; gravity alone gives about 2.3°, and a 0.05 gate drops 3°. It is shoved off the hanger, then stays near 0° instead of swinging (the 2 cm gate swings ±24°). Visual and physics are both wrong over the thickness slider (0.005 to 0.1).
findings.fix: In build_gate: drop = max(0.006, th / 2 + 0.003), then _hanger(c, y=drop + 0.006), so the hanger's underside clears the corners at any angle. The gate, spring, post and pivot stay where they are. In mechanisms-springs.js addModel('spring-gate', 'hanger'): const drop = Math.max(0.006, (ctx.props.thickness ?? 0.02) / 2 + 0.003); const pinY = -h / 2 - drop. Size the web from the knuckle up to the leaf to the gap: put(mesh(L.rbox(0.0036, drop - rb + 0.0006, lz, 0.0006), steel), 0, -h / 2 - (drop - rb) / 2 + 0.0003, 0). Mirror in web/sim/catalog-mechanisms.js build_gate (line ~382): const drop = pymax(0.006, th / 2 + 0.003); _hanger(c, { y: drop + 0.006 }). Re-run test_mechanisms.

findings.problem: The material key 'armLeather' is created twice with different parameters: the arm's cup has a leather normal map, the lip's cushion has none. kit.mat caches by key, so whichever part builds first decides how both look. Under the progressive build or a card render the order can change, and the cup can lose its leather grain.
findings.fix: In the 'lip' model, call the cushion's material 'lipLeather' (or pass the arm's full parameter set, including the normal map) so each key always means one set of parameters.

(bodyDepthOf(j.a) || bodyDepthOf(j.b)) : 0` (bodyDepthOf = the doc solid's body.depth), `const ms = Array.from({length: rows}, (_, k) => { const m = addMesh(group, geo, coilMaterial()); m.customDepthMaterial = coilDepth; m.frustumCulled = false; m.userData.z = rows > 1 ? -depth / 2 + (k + 0.5) * depth / rows : 0; return m })`, and in the updater `for (const m of ms) { m.visible = true; m.position.set(p1.x, p1.y, m.userData.z); m.rotation.z = Math.atan2(-dx, dy); m.scale.y = len }` (and `visible = false` for all when an anchor is missing). view3d.js buildPulley (Atwood / pulley lift wheels): `const single = j.render?.wheel === 'single' && two`. When single: one wheel at the midpoint C of groundA and groundB; rc (rope centre line) = |GB - GA| / 2 and the outer radius Rw = rc + 2*rho (so the vertical rope runs are exactly under the rope's tangent points T1 = GA and T4 = GB and hang straight down to the weights, not slanted); solve(): T1 = (GA.x, GA.y), T4 = (GB.x, GB.y), segs[1] hidden; wheel turn = s*(st.la - la0)/rc. Draw the plate and eye behind the wheel only (plate top at or below C.y + Rw + 0.006, no eye above the bar). Replace the dark '+' face with a recessed web and 5-6 spokes. For the two-wheel case (rope over two wheels) place wheel A at GA.x + Rw and wheel B at GB.x - Rw. Once that lands the group sets, in catalog_mechanisms.py: build_atwood wr = round(d / 2 + 0.004, 4) and the pulley joint gets render={'wheel': 'single'}; build_lift wr = round(gap + 0.004, 4) (gap = Wc/2 + sw/2 + 0.04 is already half the wheel spacing) with the same render; _rig bar y = wr + 0.012 follows by itself.

view3d.js buildSpring: when j.render?.rows > 1 draw the rows as separate meshes (z_k = -depth/2 + (k + 0.5) * depth / rows) with one shared updater, each a low-detail coil from a new `coilGeometry(turns, R, w, {perTurn: 6, radial: 4})` cached under `coil|lo|${turns}|${R}|${w}` (about 1.8k triangles for 37 turns). With the group's cap of 12 rows that is at most 24 coils, about 43k triangles. Also turns > 24 -> N = turns * 10 for single coils (hanging-spring's 72 turns are 20.7k triangles).

view3d.js buildChain / chainLinkGeometry (wrecking-ball chain, 53k-191k triangles): lower the link detail as the count rises: `const radial = n > 60 ? 5 : 6; const tub = Math.max(12, Math.min(64, 4 * Math.floor(24000 / (n * 2 * radial) / 4))); const geo = geometry(`chainlink|${rw.toFixed(5)}|${tub}|${radial}`, () => chainLinkGeometry(rw, tub, radial))` and `chainLinkGeometry(rw, tub = 64, radial = 8)` returns `new THREE.TubeGeometry(new Stadium(), tub, rw, radial, true)`. About 24k triangles for the chain at any length.
